To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrochemical and electromechanically responses of NiO2/VGC and NiO2·H2O/VGC polymer actuators were compared with those of the SWCNT and VGCF polymer actuators.

the NiO2/VGC and NiO2·H2O/VGC hybrid actuators exhibited a strain that was approximately 1.5 times greater than that exhibited by SWCNT-based actuactors, and this strain was attributable to the FC mechanism.

we developed a hybrid (EDLC/FC) actuator system using a metal oxide (Ni(O2·xH)2 or NiO2) and carbon nanofibres (VGCFs), and that the mechanism underlying the functioning the actuator system was successfully simulated using a kinetic model that accounted for the oxidizing and reducing reactions of the metal oxides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel type of polymer actuator that exhibits high strains and high response speeds.
developing hybrid polymer actuators that exhibit high strain levels at low frequencies.
the development of a hybrid polymer actuator incorporating a NiO2· xH2O/VGC F/IL electrode that is capable of exhibiting a large strain at low frequencies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the metal oxide (e.g. NiO2· xH2O) and the VGCF are essential for the fabrication of high-performance hybrid polymer
the NiO2-based actuators are superior to SWCNT-based ones in terms of strain and the frequency response.
NiO2·XH2O/Vapor Grown Carbon Fiber (VGCF)/IL electrode is a good choice for the polymer actuators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EDLC/FC hybrid system is a promising actuator for practical applications.
the EDLC/FC-based actuator systems can be used to control the electromechanical responses of the actuators by changing their electrode compositions.
the NiO2/VGF/IL actuator system is a hybrid actuator system, and that this system can be modeled using an electrochemical double-layer charging kinetic equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EDLC/FC actuator system is a new type of electrochemical actuator, and its performance is significantly superior to that of EDLC-based actuators.

the use of NiO2·H2O or anhydrous NiO2 as an active component in polymer actuator systems can improve the performance of the devices and that the use of the double-layer charging kinetic equation to simulate the electromechanical response of polymer actuators is a useful tool for predicting the strains of the devices and for designing actuators that exhibit high performance.

the EDLC and FC mechanisms can be combined in an actuator system, and that the strain levels of the resulting devices can be controlled by adjusting the amount of the metal oxide in the actuator system.
